name: Halloween
seo_title: Halloween Charcuterie Board Ideas (Adults, Kids + Cups)
description: Halloween charcuterie board ideas for adults and kids: a spooky grown-up board, a kids' board, charcuterie cups, pumpkin and spiderweb shapes, and how much to buy.
answer: The best Halloween charcuterie board keeps the food good and lets the color do the spooky work: orange cheddar, black olives and blackberries, dark crackers and blood-red salami. Make a grown-up board with a sharp cheese and a bold drink, a kids' board with mild cheese and candy, or portable charcuterie cups for a party that moves around.

ideas.title: The Grown-Up Spooky Board
ideas.text: Aged cheddar and bright-orange Mimolette, spicy soppressata and chorizo, blood oranges, black grapes and dark charcoal crackers. Serve with a smoky mezcal or a dark stout.

ideas.title: The Kids' Monster Board
ideas.text: Mild cheddar and pepper-free salami cut with Halloween cookie cutters, pretzels as broomsticks, apples, grapes and a little candy corn for the final touch.

ideas.title: Halloween Charcuterie Cups
ideas.text: A skewer of salami and cheese, three crackers and a few olives or grapes in a 9 oz clear cup. Wrap the cup in orange or black paper or draw a jack-o'-lantern face on it.

shapes.name: Jack-o'-Lantern Board
steps: Use a round board. Fill the whole circle with orange: cheddar cubes, dried apricots and mandarin segments.
Make the eyes and mouth with black olives, blackberries or dark crackers.
Add a stem of rosemary or a green pepper at the top.

shapes.name: Spiderweb Board
steps: Pipe or spoon a web of sour cream or labneh over a round dip, or lay pretzel sticks as the web lines.
Fill the spaces between the lines with salami, cheese and crackers.
Finish with one 'spider' made of a black olive and pretzel legs.

shapes.name: Cauldron Board
steps: Set a small black pot or bowl of dip in the center: pimento cheese or a green herb dip.
Circle it with dippers: crackers, pretzels and breadsticks.
Surround the circle with meat, cheese and grapes, like fire under the pot.

plan.what: Pick your board and buy cups, cookie cutters and any decorations.
Shop for cheese, meat, crackers and fruit. Buy crackers in sealed sleeves so they stay crisp.
Cut cheese shapes and fold meats. Keep them covered in the fridge.
Take cheese out to lose its chill. Assemble cups now; they hold 2 hours.
Build the board: bowls first, then cheese, meat, crackers, fruit, then the spooky details.

faq.q: How do you make a charcuterie board spooky without ruining the food?
faq.a: Let color do the work: orange cheeses and fruit, black olives, blackberries and charcoal crackers, and one or two shapes cut with a cookie cutter. Skip food dye and fake props that touch the food.

faq.q: How much charcuterie do I need for a Halloween party?
faq.a: As an appetizer, plan about 2 oz of cheese and 2 oz of meat per guest, plus 5 to 6 crackers. If the board is the main food, double it.

faq.q: How far ahead can I make charcuterie cups?
faq.a: Up to 2 hours ahead at room temperature, or the morning of if you keep them covered in the fridge. Add crackers last so they stay crisp.
Orange cheddar, Mimolette and Red Leicester. All three are colored with annatto, a natural seed extract, and all three look right on a Halloween board.

faq.q: What should I serve with a Halloween charcuterie board?
faq.a: For adults, a dark beer, a smoky mezcal cocktail or apple cider. For kids, sparkling apple cider or orange soda in clear cups.
